titleEn: Pushing a landlord to fix damp walls
titleTh: เร่งเจ้าของห้องให้ซ่อมผนังชื้น
scenarioSentences: Your bedroom walls have been damp for weeks.
Now there is black mold near the window.
You have told your landlord twice.
His name is Mr. Fischer.
You call him again.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Mr. Fischer, it's about the damp again. There's black mold on the bedroom wall now.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Fischer
dialogue.text: I'm sorry. I've been very busy, but I'll send someone soon.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: You said that last month. Mold isn't good for my health, so it can't wait.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Fischer
dialogue.text: You're right. The builder can come next Wednesday to repair the wall.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That's still a week. What am I supposed to do until then?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Fischer
dialogue.text: I'll bring you a machine that dries the air tomorrow. It should help a bit.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Thank you. But if the repair doesn't happen next week, I'll report it to the housing office.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Fischer
dialogue.text: That's fair. I'll text you the builder's details tonight.

titleEn: Ending a phone contract early
titleTh: ขอยกเลิกสัญญามือถือก่อนกำหนด
scenarioSentences: You are moving abroad next month.
Your phone contract still has eight months left.
Ending it early costs a big fee.
Ms. Yamada works at the phone shop.
You ask her about your options.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hi. I'm moving abroad next month, so I need to end my contract early.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Yamada
dialogue.text: I see. There are eight months left, so the fee would be two hundred dollars.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That's a lot. I won't even be in the country to use the phone.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Yamada
dialogue.text: I understand. If you can prove you're moving, the fee is lower.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: What kind of proof do you need?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Yamada
dialogue.text: A work contract or a rental agreement from your new country would be fine.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I have my job offer letter. How much would I pay then?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Yamada
dialogue.text: Just fifty dollars. Bring the letter, and I'll close the account the same day.

titleEn: Deciding whether to allow a pet
titleTh: ตัดสินใจเรื่องเลี้ยงหมาในบ้าน
scenarioSentences: You share a house with Jordan.
Jordan wants to adopt a dog.
You are worried about noise and mess.
You also have exams soon.
You talk about it at dinner.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Jordan, I've been thinking about the dog. I'm not against it, but I have some worries.

dialogue.speaker: Jordan
dialogue.text: I get it. What worries you most?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Barking while I study, and hair everywhere. I don't want to clean up after it.

dialogue.speaker: Jordan
dialogue.text: I'd be responsible for everything: walks, feeding and cleaning. You wouldn't have to do anything.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: And if it barks all day while you're at work?

dialogue.speaker: Jordan
dialogue.text: How about a trial month? If it doesn't work, I'll find it another home.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Okay, a trial month, as long as the dog stays out of my room.

dialogue.speaker: Jordan
dialogue.text: Deal. I'll write the rules down so we're both clear.

titleEn: Replacing a speaker who canceled
titleTh: หาวิทยากรแทนคนที่ยกเลิก
scenarioSentences: You and Tomás run the business club together.
Your guest speaker just canceled.
The event is in two days.
Sixty students have signed up.
You call Tomás to make a plan.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Tomás, bad news. Our speaker canceled this morning. She's sick.

dialogue.speaker: Tomás
dialogue.text: Oh no, two days before? Should we postpone the whole event?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I'd rather not. Sixty people signed up, and the room is booked.

dialogue.speaker: Tomás
dialogue.text: Then we need someone fast. What about Sara? She was a member and now runs her own company.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Good idea. But she works until five, and we start at four.

dialogue.speaker: Tomás
dialogue.text: We could move the start time to six. Most students prefer evenings anyway.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: True. I'll call Sara now, and if she agrees, you email everyone about the new time.

dialogue.speaker: Tomás
dialogue.text: Sounds good. I'll prepare the email so it's ready to send.

titleEn: Dealing with an overbooked hotel
titleTh: เจอโรงแรมรับจองห้องเกิน
scenarioSentences: You arrive at your hotel late at night.
You booked and paid weeks ago.
Mr. Lambert is at the reception desk.
He says there are no rooms left.
You need a bed tonight.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I don't understand. I booked this room a month ago and paid in full.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Lambert
dialogue.text: I'm very sorry. The hotel is overbooked tonight, and there's nothing I can do here.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: It's nearly midnight. Where am I supposed to sleep?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Lambert
dialogue.text: We have an agreement with a partner hotel nearby. I can book you a room there.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Is it the same standard? I paid for a room with breakfast.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Lambert
dialogue.text: It's a similar hotel, and breakfast is included. We'll also pay for your taxi.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: All right. But I'd like a refund for tonight, since I'm not staying here.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Lambert
dialogue.text: Of course. I'll refund tonight's payment, and the taxi will be here in ten minutes.

titleEn: Reporting a stolen bike for insurance
titleTh: แจ้งประกันเรื่องจักรยานถูกขโมย
scenarioSentences: Your bike was stolen outside the gym yesterday.
It was locked to a post.
Luckily, you have home insurance.
Ms. Okoye is your insurance agent.
You call her to make a claim.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hello, Ms. Okoye. My bike was stolen outside the gym yesterday. Am I covered?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Okoye
dialogue.text: Let me check your policy. Yes, bikes are covered if they were locked.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: It was locked to a post, but they cut the lock.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Okoye
dialogue.text: Then you'll need a police report. Have you reported it yet?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Not yet. I'll go to the station this afternoon. What else do you need?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Okoye
dialogue.text: The receipt for the bike, if you still have it, or a bank statement.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I've got the receipt. How long will the claim take?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Okoye
dialogue.text: About ten days once I have both documents. Email them to me as soon as possible.

titleEn: Negotiating the price of a used car
titleTh: ต่อราคารถมือสอง
scenarioSentences: You are looking for a used car.
Mr. Kaplan is selling one for six thousand dollars.
You test-drove it this morning.
It has old tires and a small dent.
You make him an offer.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Mr. Kaplan, I like the car, but six thousand is too much for me.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Kaplan
dialogue.text: It's a fair price. The engine is in great condition.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: The engine is fine, but the tires need replacing soon, and there's that dent.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Kaplan
dialogue.text: The dent is tiny. What are you offering?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Five thousand. New tires alone will cost me about six hundred.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Kaplan
dialogue.text: That's too low. I could do fifty-five hundred, as long as you pay this week.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: If I pay by Friday, would you accept fifty-three hundred?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Kaplan
dialogue.text: Fifty-four, and that's my final offer.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Okay, fifty-four hundred. I'll transfer the money on Friday.

titleEn: Applying to sell food at a festival
titleTh: สมัครขายอาหารในงานเทศกาล
scenarioSentences: You make homemade dumplings with your cousin.
You want a food stall at the summer festival.
Ms. Lindqvist is the festival organizer.
You do not know the rules yet.
You call her to ask.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hello, Ms. Lindqvist. My cousin and I would like a stall to sell dumplings.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Lindqvist
dialogue.text: Great. The stall fee is three hundred dollars for the whole weekend.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That's more than we expected. Is there a cheaper option?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Lindqvist
dialogue.text: You could share a stall with another seller and pay half.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That could work. Are there any rules about cooking food?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Lindqvist
dialogue.text: Yes. Anyone cooking needs a food safety certificate, and raw food must be kept cold.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: We don't have a certificate yet. How long does it take to get one?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Lindqvist
dialogue.text: There's a one-day course. Get it first, then apply with a copy before May tenth.

titleEn: Planning an anniversary gift for parents
titleTh: หารเงินซื้อของขวัญวันครบรอบให้พ่อแม่
scenarioSentences: Your parents' thirtieth anniversary is next month.
You and your sister, Mei, want to buy a gift.
Mei earns much more than you.
You are still a student.
You discuss it on the phone.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Mei, about Mom and Dad's anniversary. I'd love to do something big, but I'm on a student budget.

dialogue.speaker: Mei
dialogue.text: I was thinking of a weekend trip to the mountains. It's about six hundred dollars.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That's a great idea, but I can't pay three hundred.

dialogue.speaker: Mei
dialogue.text: What if we split it by income? I earn more, so I'll pay more.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That's generous. Could I pay a third, so two hundred?

dialogue.speaker: Mei
dialogue.text: Sure. I'll cover four hundred, and you can plan the details.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Deal. I'll find a hotel and book it this week.

dialogue.speaker: Mei
dialogue.text: Perfect. Just keep it a secret until the day.

titleEn: Asking to work from home
titleTh: ขอทำงานจากที่บ้าน
scenarioSentences: You started a new office job in March.
Your commute takes ninety minutes each way.
You are often tired at work.
Your manager is Ms. Holloway.
You ask her for a meeting.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Ms. Holloway, could I work from home some days? My commute is three hours a day.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Holloway
dialogue.text: That's a long time. How many days were you thinking of?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Three days at home and two in the office, if possible.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Holloway
dialogue.text: Three is too many. The team needs you here for meetings.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I understand. Would two days at home be acceptable?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Holloway
dialogue.text: Possibly. Let's try it for one month and see how it goes.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That's fair. Which days would you prefer?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Holloway
dialogue.text: Mondays and Fridays. If your work stays on schedule, we'll make it permanent.

titleEn: Asking builders to change their hours
titleTh: ขอให้คนงานก่อสร้างเลื่อนเวลาเริ่มงาน
scenarioSentences: Builders are working next to your dorm.
The drilling starts at seven every morning.
Your final exams begin next week.
Mr. Doyle is the site manager.
You go to the site office.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Good morning, Mr. Doyle. I live in the dorm next door. The drilling starts very early.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Doyle
dialogue.text: Seven o'clock is within the legal hours, I'm afraid.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I know, but we have final exams for the next two weeks. Nobody can sleep.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Doyle
dialogue.text: I understand, but if we start later, we'll finish late and go over budget.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Could you start at nine, just for the exam period?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Doyle
dialogue.text: We could start at nine, but then we'd need to work an hour later.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That's fine, as long as the noise stops by six.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Doyle
dialogue.text: Agreed. Nine to six for two weeks. I'll put a notice in your dorm.

titleEn: Getting a faulty washing machine replaced
titleTh: ขอเปลี่ยนเครื่องซักผ้าที่เสียบ่อย
scenarioSentences: You bought a new washing machine last month.
It has already broken down twice.
The shop repaired it once.
Ms. Rossi is the shop manager.
You visit the shop to complain.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hello, Ms. Rossi. My washing machine has broken down twice in four weeks.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Rossi
dialogue.text: I'm sorry. I can send a technician to repair it again this week.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: With respect, I don't want another repair. I'd like a replacement.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Rossi
dialogue.text: Our policy is to repair first, unless the fault can't be fixed.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: It's the same fault both times. Clearly, there's something wrong with this machine.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Rossi
dialogue.text: That's a fair point. Do you have the repair report from last time?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Yes, here it is. It says the motor was replaced.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Rossi
dialogue.text: In that case, I'll approve a new machine. We'll deliver it on Thursday and take the old one away.

titleEn: Selling furniture before moving abroad
titleTh: ขายเฟอร์นิเจอร์ก่อนย้ายไปต่างประเทศ
scenarioSentences: You are moving abroad in two weeks.
You are selling your desk and bed.
You asked two hundred dollars for both.
Ethan comes to see them.
He likes them but wants a lower price.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hi, Ethan. Come in. These are the desk and the bed.

dialogue.speaker: Ethan
dialogue.text: They look good. But two hundred is a bit high for me. Would you take one twenty?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That's quite low. The bed is only two years old, and the desk is solid wood.

dialogue.speaker: Ethan
dialogue.text: True. But I'd also have to rent a van to move them.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I'd rather not go below one sixty. But I need them gone by Friday.

dialogue.speaker: Ethan
dialogue.text: If I collect them on Friday morning, would you accept one fifty?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Okay, one fifty, as long as you take both pieces and come before noon.

dialogue.speaker: Ethan
dialogue.text: Deal. I'll pay you in cash when I pick them up.

titleEn: Planning care for Grandma after surgery
titleTh: วางแผนดูแลคุณยายหลังผ่าตัด
scenarioSentences: Your grandmother had hip surgery last week.
She comes home from the hospital on Monday.
She cannot be alone for a while.
Your cousin Liam lives nearby.
You call him to make a plan.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Liam, Grandma comes home on Monday. The doctor says she needs someone with her all the time.

dialogue.speaker: Liam
dialogue.text: For how long?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: At least three weeks. My classes are online, so I can be there on weekdays.

dialogue.speaker: Liam
dialogue.text: And I'm free every weekend, so I'll take Saturdays and Sundays.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Great. But what about nights? Neither of us can stay over every night.

dialogue.speaker: Liam
dialogue.text: We could hire a night nurse. It's expensive, but it's worth it.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Agreed. If we split the cost, it's about two hundred each per week.

dialogue.speaker: Liam
dialogue.text: That's fine. I'll call the care agency tomorrow, and you tell Grandma the plan.

titleEn: Chasing late pay from a summer job
titleTh: ทวงค่าจ้างงานช่วงซัมเมอร์ที่ยังไม่ได้
scenarioSentences: You worked at a summer camp in July.
Mr. Abbott was your boss there.
He still has not paid your last month.
It is now a month late.
You call him about it.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hello, Mr. Abbott. I'm calling about my pay for July. I still haven't received it.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Abbott
dialogue.text: Really? I thought it went out weeks ago. There must have been a mistake.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Nothing has arrived. I've checked my account every day.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Abbott
dialogue.text: I'm sorry. Our office changed payment systems, and some payments got stuck.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I understand, but I need it for my rent. If it isn't paid soon, I'll report it.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Abbott
dialogue.text: There's no need for that. I'll make sure it's paid by Friday.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Thank you. Could you confirm that in writing, by email?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Abbott
dialogue.text: Yes, I'll email you today with the amount and the payment date.

titleEn: Correcting a mistake in the student newspaper
titleTh: ขอแก้ข้อผิดพลาดในหนังสือพิมพ์นักศึกษา
scenarioSentences: You write for the student newspaper.
Your article about rent prices came out today.
It said rents rose by forty percent.
The real number was fourteen percent.
You go to see Rachel, the editor.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Rachel, I made a mistake in my article. I wrote forty percent instead of fourteen.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.text: Oh no. That's a big difference. Are you sure?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Yes, I checked my notes. I must have typed it wrong.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.text: Well, the paper copies are already printed, so we can't change those.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Could we at least fix the online version today?

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.text: Yes, I'll update it this afternoon and add a note explaining the change.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Thanks. Should we also print a correction?

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.text: We should. It'll go on page two of the next issue, along with an apology.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I'm really sorry. I'll double-check every number from now on.

titleEn: Negotiating a group climbing discount
titleTh: ต่อรองส่วนลดกลุ่มที่ศูนย์ปีนผา
scenarioSentences: You are planning a club trip.
Fifteen students want to try indoor climbing.
The normal price is thirty dollars each.
Ms. Carver runs the climbing center.
You call her to ask about prices.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hello, Ms. Carver. I'd like to bring fifteen students for a climbing session. Do you offer group discounts?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Carver
dialogue.text: We do. Groups of ten or more get ten percent off.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That helps, but it's still a lot for students. Is there anything better?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Carver
dialogue.text: Which day were you thinking of?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Saturday afternoon, ideally.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Carver
dialogue.text: That's our busiest time. If you came on a weekday morning, I could give you twenty-five percent off.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Most of us have no classes on Wednesday mornings. Would that work?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Carver
dialogue.text: Yes. Wednesday at ten, and that includes shoes and an instructor.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Perfect. I'll confirm the numbers by Friday.

titleEn: Leaving a French course early
titleTh: ขอยกเลิกคอร์สภาษาฝรั่งเศสกลางคัน
scenarioSentences: You paid for an evening French course.
You have just started a new job.
Your shifts are now in the evenings.
Ms. Moreau works at the language school.
You ask her about a refund.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hi, Ms. Moreau. I got a job with evening shifts, so I can't come to class anymore.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Moreau
dialogue.text: That's good news about the job. How many classes have you attended?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Only three out of ten. Could I get a refund for the rest?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Moreau
dialogue.text: We can't refund everything after the course starts. The best I can do is half.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Half seems low, since I'll miss seven classes.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Moreau
dialogue.text: There's another option. You could move to our online class on Saturday mornings at no extra cost.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: So I'd keep the full value of the course?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Moreau
dialogue.text: Exactly. You'd finish the remaining seven lessons online.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: In that case, I'd rather switch to online. Please sign me up.

titleEn: Proposing a community garden
titleTh: เสนอทำสวนชุมชน
scenarioSentences: An empty lot on your street is full of trash.
Your neighbors want to make it a garden.
The city owns it.
Mr. Nwosu works at the city council.
You go to see him.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Mr. Nwosu, the empty lot on our street is full of trash. We'd like a garden there.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Nwosu
dialogue.text: Nice idea, but who would look after it? The city has no budget for that.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: The residents would. Twenty families have already signed up to help.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Nwosu
dialogue.text: Impressive. But the council may want to build there one day.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Could we use it until then? We'd remove everything if you needed it back.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Nwosu
dialogue.text: I could approve a one-year trial, as long as you keep it clean and safe.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That sounds fair. What do we need to do first?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Nwosu
dialogue.text: Fill in this form with a simple plan, and I'll send it to the council.

titleEn: Handling an angry customer at the bakery
titleTh: รับมือลูกค้าที่ไม่พอใจที่ร้านเบเกอรี่
scenarioSentences: You work at a bakery on weekends.
Mrs. Hale ordered a large cake for a party.
Your coworker gave her a small one.
The party starts in two hours.
She comes back, very upset.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hello, Mrs. Hale. Is something wrong with the cake?

dialogue.speaker: Mrs. Hale
dialogue.text: Yes! I ordered a large cake for thirty people. This one barely feeds ten.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I'm so sorry. Let me check your order. You're right, it was our mistake.

dialogue.speaker: Mrs. Hale
dialogue.text: The party starts in two hours. What am I supposed to do now?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: We can make a large one in about an hour. Could you wait or come back?

dialogue.speaker: Mrs. Hale
dialogue.text: An hour? I'd rather not, but I suppose I have no choice.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I'll bring it to your car myself. And we'll give you thirty percent off.

dialogue.speaker: Mrs. Hale
dialogue.text: Fine. That helps. I'll come back at four, then.
